\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{તરબૂચ} (tarbūc)}{તરબૂચ (tarbūc)}]{\gu{તરબૂચ} (tarbūc) — a watermelon}

\label{lesson:GU-C116-tarbuc}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a lemon, then the Gujarati for a coconut.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{તરબૂચ}}
\textbf{\gu{તરબૂચ}} (\emph{tarbūc}) — \textquotedblleft{}a watermelon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{તરબૂચ}} (\emph{tarbūc}) is a loan, usually traced to Persian \emph{tarbuz}, \textquotedblleft{}watermelon\textquotedblright{}. Gujarati ends it in \emph{c}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarbūc}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{tarbūc}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a lemon, then the Gujarati for a coconut, then say \emph{tarbūc} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{પપૈયું} (papaiyũ)}{પપૈયું (papaiyũ)}]{\gu{પપૈયું} (papaiyũ) — a papaya}

\label{lesson:GU-C116-papaiyu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a coconut, then the Gujarati for a watermelon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{પપૈયું}}
\textbf{\gu{પપૈયું}} (\emph{papaiyũ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a papaya\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{પપૈયું}} (\emph{papaiyũ}) is usually linked with \emph{papaya}, a Caribbean word that Spanish and Portuguese sailors carried round the world. CDIAL has no entry for it, so the road it took into Gujarati is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{જામફળ} (jāmphaḷ)}{જામફળ (jāmphaḷ)}]{\gu{જામફળ} (jāmphaḷ) — a guava}

\label{lesson:GU-C116-jamphal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a watermelon, then the Gujarati for a papaya.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{જામફળ}}
\textbf{\gu{જામફળ}} (\emph{jāmphaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a guava\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{જામફળ}} (\emph{jāmphaḷ}) appears to be \emph{jām}, which CDIAL lists as the fruit of the rose-apple tree under Sanskrit \emph{jambu} (CDIAL 5131), with \emph{phaḷ}, \textquotedblleft{}fruit\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9051). CDIAL lists a different Gujarati word for the guava, \emph{jamrukh} (CDIAL 5135).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}

\end{cousinweb}
